headline: ARIZONA GOLD PERRY ZONE GROWS: 21.79M AT 4.10 G/T AU WITHIN 73M AT 1.69 G/T — 150M VERTICAL EXTENSION AT PHILADELPHIA
snippet: Arizona Gold & Silver (TSXV: AZS) reported August 17 that hole PC26-169 at the Perry Zone of the Philadelphia Gold-Silver Project in Arizona returned 21.79 metres grading 4.10 g/t gold within a broader 73.46-metre interval averaging 1.69 g/t gold — extending the Perry Zone mineralization approximately 150 metres vertically beyond the limits of the current resource model. The result confirms continuity of high-grade gold-silver mineralization at depth in a zone that is now growing both laterally and vertically with successive drill holes. At $4,400 gold and $65 silver, an Arizona-jurisdiction gold-silver discovery with a vertical extent now demonstrably open at depth and a high-grade core of 4.10 g/t over 21+ metres represents a compelling resource growth story: the gap between the current resource model and where the drill bit is finding high-grade gold is the specific valuation gap that exploration-stage retail investors are positioned to capture.

headline: MITHRIL SILVER & GOLD COPALQUIN MRE JUMPS 196%: 343K OZ AU + 8.479 MOZ AG INDICATED — MEXICO DISTRICT NOW 464K AUEQ
snippet: Mithril Silver & Gold (TSXV: MSG) delivered a 196% resource upgrade at Copalquin Target 1 in the Durango State, Mexico — increasing the Indicated Resource to 464,000 gold-equivalent ounces, comprising 343,000 ounces of gold and 8.479 million ounces of silver. A 196% resource growth in a single estimate update is an extraordinary outcome for a junior silver-gold developer: it means the resource has more than tripled from its prior estimate, moving Copalquin from a speculative exploration target toward a project with the scale required to underpin a preliminary economic assessment. Mexico's Durango State is historically one of the most prolific silver-gold mining districts in the world, hosting major producing mines at similar geological styles. For retail investors tracking the silver space at $65 per ounce, a junior with 8.479 million silver ounces in Indicated Resources — now confirmed via NI 43-101 — represents the specific category of asset that junior silver majors have historically acquired as the commodity cycle matures.

headline: GOLD HOLDS $4,380 AS FOMC MINUTES WEDNESDAY AND WARSH'S JACKSON HOLE DEBUT LOOM — 35% SEPTEMBER HIKE ODDS THE BINARY
snippet: Gold traded near $4,380 on August 18 as markets positioned ahead of two near-term binary catalysts: the release of the July 28-29 FOMC meeting minutes on Wednesday August 19, and Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's inaugural Jackson Hole address on August 28 — his first as Fed Chair since replacing Jerome Powell in May 2026. The July FOMC vote was 9-3 in favour of holding, with three dissenters pressing for an immediate rate hike — a more hawkish internal split than prior meetings. Options markets currently assign approximately 35% probability to a September rate hike, down sharply from the 50%+ probability that prevailed before August's run of soft economic data. For gold investors, the Wednesday FOMC minutes are the immediate test: if the minutes reveal a broader hawkish drift beyond the three formal dissenters, rate-hike probability reprices upward and gold faces a tactical headwind into a still-overcrowded speculative positioning structure. The constructive base case — neutral or dovish minutes plus a measured Warsh Jackson Hole — would clear the path for gold to challenge the $4,424 CPI-day high established August 12.

headline: GOLDGROUP MINING DON DAVID H1 2026: 25,726M IN 123 HOLES — SADIE 1 HITS 26.78 G/T AUEQ OVER 1.92M ETW IN OAXACA
snippet: Goldgroup Mining (TSXV: GORO) reported August 17 that its H1 2026 drill program at the Don David Gold Mine in Oaxaca, Mexico totalled 25,726 metres across 123 holes — a substantial program for a producing junior, combining resource expansion, exploration, and infill drilling across multiple zones. The standout intercept from the period: the Sadie 1 exploration zone returned 1.92 metres estimated true width grading 26.78 g/t gold equivalent (13.49 g/t gold, 931 g/t silver) — a very high-grade hit in a new target outside the current mine plan. Don David is a producing gold-silver mine with a long operating history in Oaxaca; the combination of active production and a 25,000+ metre exploration drill program feeding into multiple discovery zones — including a 26.78 g/t AuEq intercept in a step-out target — positions Goldgroup as a small producer with meaningful resource-growth optionality at $4,400 gold and $65 silver. For retail investors evaluating Mexican junior producers, Oaxaca-jurisdiction gold-silver operations with active drilling carry both the upside of new discovery and the execution risk of Mexico's evolving mining regulatory environment.

headline: ALICE QUEEN LAUNCHES 5,000M DRILL AT HORN ISLAND GOLD — 569K OZ JORC MRE IN QUEENSLAND, FIRST HOLES TARGET RESOURCE EXTENSION
snippet: Alice Queen (ASX: AQX) announced August 17 the commencement of a 5,000-metre reverse-circulation drill program at the Horn Island Gold Project in Far North Queensland — targeting extensions to the existing 569,000-ounce JORC Mineral Resource Estimate and testing new geological targets identified through recent structural reinterpretation. Horn Island is the only gold project on Horn Island, located in the Torres Strait — a logistically unique but operationally manageable setting given the project's proximity to Thursday Island infrastructure. The 569,000-ounce existing resource provides the anchor for an Australian-jurisdiction gold developer pursuing a resource growth strategy at a time when AUD gold prices are at levels not seen in modern mining history. For ASX-listed junior gold investors evaluating Far North Queensland exposure, the Horn Island drill launch is a straightforward resource-extension catalyst: each hole reported against a 569,000-ounce baseline has an explicit mathematical relationship to any revised resource estimate, giving investors a concrete framework for tracking program success.

headline: SILVER'S NEW ERA: 762 MOZ CUMULATIVE DEFICIT SINCE 2021 — SILVER INSTITUTE PROJECTS ANOTHER 46.3 MOZ SHORTFALL IN 2026
snippet: Money Metals Exchange's August 15 analysis documents the structural supply-demand imbalance driving silver's 2026 bull case: six consecutive annual supply deficits have produced a cumulative shortfall of 762 million ounces since 2021 — an amount roughly equivalent to ten months of global annual production that has been drawn from above-ground stockpiles. The Silver Institute's 2026 forecast projects a further deficit of 46.3 million ounces this year, driven simultaneously by record industrial demand (solar photovoltaic fabrication alone will consume an estimated 232 million ounces in 2026) and a supply side that cannot respond quickly to elevated prices given the long lead times for silver mine development and the fact that 70-75% of silver is produced as a byproduct of base metal mining. At $65 silver, the gap between cost of production for primary silver miners (typically $16-22 per ounce AISC) and spot price is historically wide — creating the free-cash-flow-per-ounce economics that should attract capital into the sector. The 762-million-ounce cumulative draw is Money Metals' core argument for why silver's structural floor is rising: those stockpiles cannot be indefinitely liquidated, and the market will eventually need to incentivise new primary silver mine production at a price level that justifies the 7-12 year development timelines involved.

headline: COPPER RETREATS TO $6.55/LB AS LME INVENTORIES TIGHTEN BELOW 205K TONNES — ICSG FLIPS TO 150K MT 2026 DEFICIT FORECAST
snippet: Copper pulled back toward $6.55 per pound in mid-August 2026 after its record run above $6.90, with LME warehouse inventories declining below 205,000 tonnes — roughly half of which are earmarked for near-term withdrawal — as physical tightness persisted despite the futures price correction. The International Copper Study Group revised its 2026 supply-demand balance to a 150,000-metric-tonne deficit, abandoning the marginal surplus forecast it had maintained through early 2026. The ICSG revision is significant: it represents the organization's formal acknowledgment that AI data centre construction, grid electrification, and defence procurement demand has structurally exceeded its earlier modelling. A $6.55/lb copper pullback after a record high, against confirmed structural deficit fundamentals and LME inventory drawdowns, is the classic volatility pattern that copper bull markets exhibit — high-conviction institutional buyers accumulate into dips while speculative longs shake out. For TSX-V and ASX copper development projects whose capital cost estimates were calculated at $3.50-$4.00 copper, the current $6.55 price floor transforms project economics in ways that technical studies from 24 months ago cannot capture.

headline: ATHABASCA URANIUM BASIN: 100,000M DRILLING IN 2026, $420M+ RAISED — SPOT $87.45/LB AS UTILITY CONTRACTING ACCELERATES
snippet: Crux Investor's August 2026 Athabasca Basin sector review documents the largest coordinated uranium exploration campaign in the basin's history: over 100,000 metres of drilling across multiple active programs in the 2026 summer season, with the junior uranium sector having raised in excess of $420-450 million in equity financing since late 2024 to fund the programs. Uranium spot is trading at $87.45 per pound — up approximately 20% year-over-year — as US, European, and Japanese utilities accelerate long-term contracting to reduce dependence on Kazakh and Russian supply. NexGen Energy's Rook I development — the largest new uranium mine under active construction globally — provides the basin's proof-of-concept anchor: a world-class discovery made by a junior explorer in the Athabasca Basin that is now advancing toward production with a fully-funded construction program. CanAlaska's West McArthur Pike Zone step-out results (August 17, 350 metres both ways), Premier American Uranium's 59% hit rate at Kaycee (Wyoming, announced same day), and the broader $420M equity-raise figure collectively describe a uranium exploration industry that is simultaneously better-funded and more drilling-active than at any point since the 2007 cycle peak. For retail uranium investors, the combination of $87.45 spot price, accelerating utility contracting, and Rook I construction progress represents the most structurally complete uranium bull case since 2007.
